audits.title: P-BN37 Audit of the Management of Gall Bladder (GB) Polyps according to European Joint Guidelines (EJG), 2017
audits.standard: European Joint Guidelines (2017) on management and follow-up of gallbladder polyps

cycle1.period: Since 2017 guideline publication (ten year retrospective cohort)
cycle1.result: 36% managed according to guidelines; adherence 62% at 3 years post introduction compared with an average of 35%.

audits.other_findings: Adherence better for polyps over 10mm (p < 0.01) and when straight to laparoscopic cholecystectomy; surveillance adherence poor. No difference surgeons versus non-surgeons (p = 0.32).
audits.citation: Karunanithy V, Richardson T, Kumar A, Thomas S, Khan S. P-BN37 Audit of the Management of Gall Bladder (GB) Polyps according to European Joint Guidelines (EJG), 2017. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab430.035.

audits.title: OGBN P11 Gallbladder polyps: an audit of management in an NHS trust
audits.standard: Joint ESGAR/EAES/EFISDS/ESGE guidelines on gallbladder polyp management
audits.setting: Torbay and South Devon NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 86% appropriately offered surgery for polyps ≥10 mm; 40% with polyps >5 mm and risk factors not offered cholecystectomy; 44% without risk factors not offered appropriate follow-up; all without risk factors with polyps ≤5 mm appropriately managed.

audits.intervention: Recommended unified local or national guidelines and multidisciplinary consensus.
audits.other_findings: Most patients with polyps ≤5 mm and risk factors were not offered ultrasound surveillance.
audits.citation: Frank A, Halaseh S, Platt T. OGBN P11 Gallbladder polyps: an audit of management in an NHS trust. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac404.056.

audits.title: 691 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance Audit
audits.standard: ESGAR/EASES/EFISDS/ESGE joint guidelines (6, 12 and 24 monthly scans for 6-9mm polyps; cholecystectomy >10mm); local trust guideline of 12 and 24 monthly scans
audits.setting: District general hospital (Lister Hospital / West Suffolk Hospital); ultrasound-diagnosed gallbladder polyps

cycle1.result: Of 82 (36.6%) 6-9mm polyps, 62 (75%) followed up; mean time to second scan 472 days, median 556 days; timing not within recommended guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Correct scan modality used; 17 had cholecystectomy with 1 malignancy; 14 polyps increased in size.
audits.citation: Tabassum T, Khrais M. 691 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.134.

audits.title: BN SO29 - Overinvestigation and unnecessary surgery for Gallbladder Polyps: An audit of compliance with ESGAR guidelines
audits.standard: 2021 ESGAR guidance on management of gallbladder polyps
audits.setting: East Surrey Hospital, single NHS Trust in England

cycle1.result: 35 (36%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, including all with polyp >10mm; histology cholecystitis 69%, true gallbladder polyp 6%; 47% of symptomatic patients had two ultrasounds and two clinic appointments. Adherence to ESGAR was inconsistent.

audits.other_findings: 74% (26/35) of cholecystectomy patients had biliary symptoms and 77% (20/26) of these had cholecystitis on histology.
audits.citation: Blackburn J, Farksas N, Crotty F, Miller F, Belgaumkar A. BN SO29 - Overinvestigation and unnecessary surgery for Gallbladder Polyps: An audit of compliance with ESGAR guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae271.200.

audits.title: 221 Follow-Up for Patients with Radiologically Diagnosed Gallbladder Polyps in Primary Care: A 2-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: Local commissioning group (2019) primary care guidance on interval ultrasound for gallbladder polyps

cycle1.result: 30/72 (41.6%) lost to follow-up; 31/72 (43.1%) complied with guidance; 11/72 (15.3%) due appointments within guidelines.

audits.intervention: Invitation for repeat imaging or consultation with a doctor.
audits.other_findings: Median 36 months overdue (IQR 45.5); Indian ethnicity was associated with 46.6% greater average polyp size.
audits.citation: Hazell G, Rinson J, De Silva R. 221 Follow-Up for Patients with Radiologically Diagnosed Gallbladder Polyps in Primary Care: A 2-Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.223.

audits.title: 856 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance at MFT Hospitals: Audit of Current Practice Against Latest Guidelines
audits.standard: 2021 joint European guidelines on gallbladder polyp surveillance
audits.setting: 8 Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust hospitals

cycle1.result: 17% of patient pathways adhered to the guidelines; 14% adherent for patients with risk factors; 58 unnecessary scans and 35 missed cholecystectomy referrals.

audits.intervention: Recommended: single guideline distribution, inclusion of unacknowledged size thresholds and a standardised radiology reporting template.
audits.other_findings: 63% of ultrasound reports did not document gallstones, 35% did not document wall thickness and 0% documented polyp sessility.
audits.citation: Manghnani J. 856 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance at MFT Hospitals: Audit of Current Practice Against Latest Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.480.
